title: Linking through student ID
description: Student ID is transmitted in the data flow, enabling linking of data across systems based on a unique identifier.
assumptions: Student ID is a globally unique identifier within the educational system.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of student ID, course, and file reference can serve as quasi-identifiers that may link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes may be unique or near-unique to individual students.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The data flow processes identified information including student ID, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Student ID is personally identifiable information.

title: Identifier in data flow
description: Student ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject transmitted in the data flow.
assumptions: Student ID serves as a direct identifier for the student.

title: Quasi-identifier in data flow
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference constitutes quasi-identifiers that may allow identification of the data subject.
assumptions: These attributes together may uniquely identify a student within the system context.

title: Data propagation to service
description: Personal data is propagated from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service where it may not be strictly needed.
assumptions: The Assignment & Grading Service may have access to more data than functionally required for its role.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (P1 and P2) which may exceed functional necessity.
assumptions: The data sharing between P1 and P2 is known at design time and may be broader than needed.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission data including file references and role information is being transmitted to the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate the extent of data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the quality of privacy notices and user awareness.

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: Students may lack control over how their submission data is processed and shared with the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Users may not have granular control over data sharing preferences.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the system's consent and preference mechanisms.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The data flow may include more personal data than functionally needed for the submission and grading process.
assumptions: File reference and requesting role may be more granular than necessary for the core functionality.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual functional requirements of the system.

title: Unique identifier linking through student ID
description: The assignment store contains student ID which is a unique identifier that can be used to link the stored assignment data to a specific student identity.
assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified data containing student ID, course, and submission time which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Student ID directly identifies the student

title: Identifier in stored data
description: The assignment store contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject through the student ID field.
assumptions: Student ID is stored in plaintext or reversible format

title: Data evidence for non-repudiation
description: The stored assignment record with student ID can be used to prevent a student from denying their submission or claims related to the assignment.
assumptions: The assignment record is tamper-evident or cryptographically secured

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Student ID is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the grading functionality.
assumptions: Student ID is more sensitive than necessary for basic assignment storage

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Assignment data may be retained longer than functionally needed for grading purposes, potentially exceeding storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: No clear retention policy exists for assignment submissions
uncertainty_note: Assumption about retention policy not confirmed from flow description

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system processes student ID, course, and submission time which may exceed what is strictly necessary for the grading functionality.
assumptions: Student ID could potentially be pseudonymized while maintaining grading functionality

title: Linking through student name identifier
description: Student names in the submission data serve as unique identifiers that can link the work content and submission times to specific students within the school context.
assumptions: Student names are unique within the school system and can be used to identify specific individuals.

title: Quasi-identifier combination linking
description: The combination of student name, work content, and submission times creates a quasi-identifier set that can uniquely identify students even without additional data.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is sufficiently unique to identify individual students.

title: Profiling through work content analysis
description: Work content can be analyzed to profile student performance, learning patterns, or behavioral characteristics, potentially linking data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Teachers or systems may analyze work content for patterns that reveal information about the student.

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal explicitly processes and displays identified student information including names, work content, and submission times.
assumptions: Student names are personally identifiable information that directly identifies the data subject.

title: Student name as identifier
description: Student names serve as unique references to the identity of the data subject in the submission data.
assumptions: Student names are unique identifiers within the school context.

title: Revealing attributes in submission data
description: The combination of name, work content, and submission times reveals multiple attributes that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Multiple attributes together provide sufficient information to identify the student.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Student names and work content are sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than strictly required for basic grade portal functionality.
assumptions: Some educational contexts may not require full student names or detailed work content to be displayed.

title: Fine-grained data disclosure
description: The data disclosed includes granular information (specific work content, exact submission times) that may be more detailed than necessary.
assumptions: Aggregated or less detailed data might suffice for teacher review purposes.

title: Predetermined party access
description: Student data is made accessible to teachers, a predetermined set of parties, which may exceed functional necessity depending on the educational context.
assumptions: Not all teachers may need access to all student submissions.

title: Student unawareness of data sharing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data (names, work content, times) is being displayed to teachers through the portal.
assumptions: Students may not have clear visibility into how their data is being shared and displayed.

title: Lack of student control over data processing
description: Students may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their submission data is processed and displayed to teachers.
assumptions: Students typically have limited control over educational data processing in institutional systems.

title: Data minimization principle violation
description: The processing of student names, work content, and submission times may exceed what is actually needed for the functional goal of displaying grades and submissions.
assumptions: Less granular data might suffice for the intended functionality.

title: Potential invalid consent for data processing
description: Student consent for data collection and processing may not be valid or clearly obtained, particularly for displaying personal data to teachers.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms in educational systems may not meet strict regulatory requirements.

title: Linking through parent-child account identifiers
description: Parent account is linked to child account, enabling linking of parent's access to child's educational data through unique identifier relationships
assumptions: Parent-child account linkage is implemented in the system

title: Quasi-identifier combining parent and child data
description: Combination of parent account attributes and child grade data can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data across individuals
assumptions: Multiple parent-child relationships exist in the system

title: Processing of identified parent and child data
description: The system requests and processes identified data including parent login credentials and child's grade information
assumptions: Parent account contains identifying information about the parent

title: Unique identifier in parent account
description: Parent account contains unique references to the identity of the parent data subject
assumptions: Parent accounts use unique identifiers (username, email, etc.)

title: Quasi-identifier through parent-child relationship
description: Combination of parent and child identifiers can uniquely identify specific parent-child relationships
assumptions: Parent-child relationships are unique within the school system

title: Sensitive grade data collection
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly required for the login and grade viewing functionality
assumptions: Grades contain more sensitive information than necessary for basic grade viewing

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: The system may analyze or process grade data beyond what is needed for the parent to view their child's grades
assumptions: System may perform analytics or store grades longer than needed

title: Child unawareness of grade access
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their grades are being accessed by the parent through this data flow
assumptions: Child does not have direct control over parent's access to their grades

title: Lack of data subject control over data processing
description: The child data subject lacks control over how their grade data is processed, accessed, and shared with the parent
assumptions: Child cannot set preferences or consent to parent's grade access

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (grades, parent-child relationship) is processed than is actually needed for the stated functionality of viewing grades
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies to this educational system

title: Unique student identifiers in account records
description: Account records written to the directory contain unique references to student identity (e.g., student IDs, account IDs) that can be used to identify specific individuals.

title: Quasi-identifiers in account records
description: Account records may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., name, date of birth, course enrollment) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify students.

title: Linking through unique student identifiers
description: The unique identifiers in account records (student IDs, account IDs) can be used to link data across different systems or contexts, potentially revealing connections between different data sources.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination

title: Potentially sensitive data types collected
description: Account records may contain sensitive personal data (grades, academic performance, parent-child relationships) that could be perceived as more sensitive than strictly required for the grading service functionality.

title: Data propagation to data store
description: Personal data is written to the account directory data store, making it accessible to other services or systems that may not need this data, increasing exposure risk.

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be aware that their account records and parent-child relationship links are being written to the account directory by the grading service.

title: Lack of student control over data processing
description: Students may not have control to set preferences or consent regarding how their account data is processed, stored, or linked in the account directory.

title: Limited rectification and erasure control
description: Students may lack control to rectify incorrect account data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant for the grading service.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The grading service may be processing more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of assignment and grading, including parent-child relationship links that may not be essential.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Account records may be stored in the directory longer than functionally needed for the grading service, potentially exceeding retention requirements.
